title: Redaction failure modes and the unredact channel that covers each (#1592)
rationale: A redaction fails in a bounded number of ways. This registry is the list, and
for each one the CHANNEL that recovers it, the EVIDENCE that the channel works,
and — where there is no channel — the issue tracking the gap.
It exists because 'unredact has eight channels' says nothing about coverage.
The question a user has is 'will it find MY leak', and that is answered per
failure mode, not per channel. A mode with no channel is the most valuable row
here: it is where excise reports a document clean that is not.
status: covered   — a channel handles it and a named test proves so
partial   — a channel handles part of it; the note says which part is not
gap       — no working channel; the issue column tracks it
A row may NAME a channel and still be a gap: the channel constant exists so
the report can say the channel did not run and why, which is the honest
output for an unimplemented one. STATUS is the authority on coverage, never
the presence of a channel name.

modes.description: An opaque box drawn over text in the page content stream; the glyphs are untouched.
producers: the most common real-world failure (Manafort, TSA, NYT/NSA, Meta/FTC, DOJ 2025)

modes.description: The covering box is a /Square or /Highlight ANNOTATION, not page content. The mark is detected; the text under it is not reported, because the hidden-text detector walks the page content stream and an annotation is not in it.
modes.note: Closed by the mark-region channel (#1606), which reads the page inside an annotation-derived mark instead of watching draw order. Before it, the mark appeared with outcome not-recovered while the text was trivially extractable — a false 'the redaction held'.

modes.description: Text and/or the covering box live inside a Form XObject the page invokes with Do.
modes.note: HiddenTextDetector's own docstring defers Form XObject recursion. FormXObjectFlattener exists on the redaction side and is not used by the audit.

modes.description: The covering fill is light, or the text is drawn in a colour close to the fill, so it is invisible without being covered.
modes.note: Contrast pairing is handled (#1131). TRANSPARENCY is not: an ExtGState /ca alpha is not tracked, so a semi-transparent box is judged by its nominal colour.

modes.description: Text drawn with Tr 3 (invisible). Fully extractable, never painted. This is how every OCR layer is written.
modes.note: Closed by #1607: ContentStreamWalker now tracks Tr through the q/Q text-state snapshot and carries it on WalkedGlyph and Letter, and HiddenTextDetector pairing D reports glyphs that paint nothing (modes 3 and 7). Before it, Tr was parsed and discarded as write-only state.

modes.description: A /Redact annotation marks an intention that was never applied; the text is untouched and the annotation says where to look.
modes.note: This row claimed covered on the strength of a test that only asserted the MARK was detected, not that the text came back — and the tier-A bench caught the overstatement. The mark-region channel makes the claim true.

modes.description: A page rasterised to an image, with the original OCR text layer left behind it.
modes.note: The differential recovers text from PIXELS under an obstruction. It does not read an existing invisible text layer — that is text-render-mode-3 above.

modes.description: Glyphs removed from a TJ array while the kerning numbers stay, so the surviving glyphs' positions encode what was between them (Bland et al., PETS 2023).
modes.note: The WIDTH budget is implemented (two-anchor gaps and the #1140 box width). The NEIGHBOUR-SHIFT half of Bland et al. is not; it lands in #1589.

modes.description: A box drawn over an image; the image XObject is intact underneath.
A box over vector artwork — a signature, a chart, a map. No text is involved, so a text-only audit reports the page clean.
The page is repointed at a redacted image while the ORIGINAL image object stays in the file, unreferenced but present.
producers: editors that add rather than replace
modes.note: Closed by #1608. Gated on a same-dimensions image being REFERENCED — the signature of a swap. Without that, an orphan is ordinary incremental-update debris and belongs to the prior-revision channel.

modes.description: The original image is retained and hidden via a soft mask (/SMask) that makes it transparent, rather than being removed.
modes.note: An all-zero 8-bit /SMask is detected. NOT detected: an /ExtGState /ca 0 drawing the image transparently, and masks in other bit depths or colour spaces — those need alpha tracking in the walker, which the box-light-or-low-contrast row also wants.

modes.description: The redaction is an incremental update; the unredacted revision is still at the front of the file and a truncation at an earlier %%EOF yields it whole.
modes.note: excise's own output is a fresh full rewrite (#586), so this is for other tools' output.

modes.description: /Thumb holds a pre-rendered picture of the page from before the redaction.
producers: editors that do not regenerate thumbnails

modes.description: An attachment carried inside the document, untouched by a page redaction.
producers: any producer; attachments are orthogonal to page content

modes.description: An AcroForm field's /V survives behind a blanked appearance and is re-painted by any reader honouring /NeedAppearances.
producers: form flatteners that blank the appearance only

modes.description: An XFA form's XML data packet still holds the field values a page redaction removed.
modes.note: Closed by #1609. XfaXmlCarrier's locator and XML loader are shared with the read mirror, so there is one source of truth for where XFA lives. A packet that will not parse is REPORTED as unexamined, never treated as clean.

modes.description: /ActualText, /Alt or /E on a StructElem restates the removed text.
The same carriers, inline in the content stream as a BDC property list — a different carrier the structure-tree walk never reaches.
modes.note: Both the inline and the NAMED property-list form are read. The scrub side cannot remove the named form (#1599), so a leak reported here survives a re-redaction.

modes.description: /Info, XMP /Metadata and outline titles restating a removed term.
modes.note: DELIBERATE: CarrierTextRecovery covers the hidden-readable carriers and excludes bulk /Info + XMP, because dumping them would bury a real leak in ordinary document metadata. PdfDocumentSanitizer scrubs them (#608); the audit does not enumerate them.
